customManagers.description: Tool versions pinned in a workflow `with:` input, annotated with a `# renovate:` comment on the preceding line (no built-in manager reads action inputs)

packageRules.description: tools/go.mod (the generators behind make generate) gets its own group, so its updates keep automerging while those of the root go.mod wait for a maintainer (rule after the automerge one): Renovate automerges a grouped branch only when every update in it is automerged. No job that holds a secret builds this module. Its commits are typed chore: nothing in it is linked into the binary, and the require depType would otherwise get fix from config:recommended and publish a provider release for each bump.

Go toolchain and indirect module updates change the shipped binary like direct ones, so they get the fix type and semantic-release publishes a patch release with them. The :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers preset of config:recommended gives fix to the require depType only, chore (no release) to the rest. Root go.mod only: tools/go.mod feeds make generate and is not linked into the binary.

No upstream release notes in an automerged PR: its description becomes the body of the squash commit on main, which semantic-release reads with no maintainer in between, and a BREAKING CHANGE line written upstream would land in the release notes and CHANGELOG.md (.releaserc keeps it from cutting a major). The reviewed rules below turn the notes back on, for the maintainer who reads them before merging.

Root go.mod updates (direct and indirect modules, and the Go toolchain) are compiled into the acceptance tests, which run with the acctest keys on the push to main that the merge makes (make testacc, make terraform-test). Never automerged, whatever the update type, so a maintainer decides on each one before that run.

tflint is installed from a pinned release zip whose sha256 is hardcoded next to the version (security.yml); Renovate can bump the version but not the hash, so its PR always fails the tflint job until TFLINT_SHA256 is updated by hand. Never automerge it (#241 was merged with the job red).

Release tooling runs next to the release credentials: the semantic-release App token, which bypasses the main ruleset, and the GPG key that signs the Registry checksums. The actions of testacc.yml run next to the acctest keys, on every push to main. Their updates get their own group and are never automerged, whatever the update type, so a maintainer reviews each one. Matched by file, so it covers the semantic-release packages and their lockfile (npm) and the actions those three workflows use (github-actions); GoReleaser (custom.regex), declared in goreleaser-release.yml too, is moved out of this group by the next rule, which matches it by name and comes later; the same action in other workflows keeps its usual automerged group. A new workflow whose jobs read any secret other than GITHUB_TOKEN, or run in a protected environment, joins this list. The commit type is forced to chore: the npm manager gives the semantic-release packages the dependencies depType, which config:recommended would title fix(deps), and a fix title would publish a provider patch release for a tooling bump.

GoReleaser is pinned twice, in goreleaser-release.yml (above) and in goreleaser-check.yml, which validates .goreleaser.yml on every PR. Both pins move in this group's single reviewed PR, separate from the release tooling group so that its red hash check, until the hash is updated by hand, holds back no other release tooling update. They must move together: otherwise the check job validates .goreleaser.yml with a different GoReleaser than the release job runs, and a config change it accepts can fail at tag time, after the GitHub release and the tag already exist. Both are env values of an install step, annotated with a # renovate: comment and read by the custom regex manager; each file also hardcodes GORELEASER_SHA256, which Renovate cannot bump, so the PR goes red in goreleaser-check.yml until a maintainer updates the hash in both files (the release job runs the binary next to the signing key, so its bytes are pinned, not only its version).

The Terraform CLI is pinned in mise.toml (mise manager, depName terraform), which terraform.yml reads to install the CLI on every pull request, and twice in testacc.yml (custom.regex, depName hashicorp/terraform) next to TERRAFORM_SHA256. Left to their own groups the two drift: the mise one automerges after three days while the testacc.yml one waits in the release tooling group for its hash. Both move in this group's single reviewed PR, so the offline checks of a pull request and the live tests on main run the same Terraform; it goes red in the terraform-digest job of security.yml until a maintainer sets TERRAFORM_SHA256 in both jobs of testacc.yml, and being a group of its own that red check holds back no other release tooling update. After the release tooling rule, which matches testacc.yml by file.

Hold anthropic-sdk-go on v1 until #192 is done in major/2.0.0: v2 moves the client to API version 2026-10-21, which is breaking for this provider (temperature, api_keys.workspace_id and the rate-limit group_type are removed, skills come back in their GA shape only, and the API key is sent as Authorization: Bearer instead of x-api-key). v1 minor and patch releases stay allowed. Remove this rule as part of #192, not on its own.

Review every anthropic-sdk-go minor release before it merges, in its own PR: v1 minors have changed what goes over the wire without breaking the build (v1.68.0 stopped sending the skills beta header, v1.75.0 started sending extra input_schema keys, v1.80.0 turned multiagent into a union), and no check on a PR calls the live API. Its own PR, so that the routine Go dependencies PR can be merged while an SDK minor waits for a closer look. Patch releases stay in that group; like every root go.mod update, neither is automerged.
Never propose a major SDK update, OSV vulnerability-fix PRs included (their allowedVersions replaces any hold above): a new major is the #192 migration, not a dependency bump.

Hold conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits below 9: 10.x needs conventional-changelog-writer@9, but the latest stable @semantic-release/release-notes-generator (14.1.1) pins writer ^8, so generateNotes fails with 'Missing helper'. Lift once release-notes-generator 15 ships with writer 9.
